content.text:
I've confirmed the exact origin of the bug.

## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: 2a5df16ac0d3576a62440a0da4818833df5cd8e5

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I started from the fix diff, which changes two occurrences of `sourceNode.getChildren(...)` / `sourceNode.keySequence.iterator()` to `source.currentNode.getChildren(...)` / `source.currentNode.keySequence.iterator()` inside the private `reclaim(...)` method of `PatriciaTreeMutable.java`. I used `git log -p --follow` on that file to find when the `sourceNode` local variable was first introduced in this method, and found it in commit `2a5df16` (Sep 14, 2016), a large refactor of GC/reclaim logic across the environment module.

**(2) The faulty change:** In `2a5df16`, the method was refactored to cache `final NodeBase actualNode = actual.currentNode;` and `final NodeBase sourceNode = source.currentNode;` once at the top of the method, presumably as a minor cleanup/optimization. However, inside the loop body, after the `else if (actItr.hasNext())` branch calls `source.moveDown()`, `source.currentNode` is mutated to point to the new (child) node — but the code kept reading from the stale cached `sourceNode` variable on the next iteration (`srcItr = sourceNode.keySequence.iterator();` and `sourceNode.getChildren(...)`) instead of re-reading `source.currentNode`. This caused the traversal to use the wrong (parent-level, stale) node's key sequence/children after moving down the tree — a classic "cached stale reference after mutation" bug.

**(3) Supporting evidence:** The fix commit `04b514d` reverts precisely these two lines back to `source.currentNode...`, with no other logic changes — confirming that the two specific usages added in `2a5df16` were the defect. The `actualNode` variable (also cached in the same commit) is used safely because the corresponding branch re-derives `actItr = actual.currentNode.keySequence.iterator()` after `actual.moveDown()`, i.e., only the `source`-side caching was inconsistent, matching exactly what the fix corrects. I'm confident this is the introducing commit, as the buggy variable and its exact faulty usages trace directly to this single commit with no intervening changes to that code path.
